value.body:
Add a built-in wall-time clock, in this diff. Jack Heart (2026-11-12): "Yeah I think we should add just wall time as a built-in clock"; "And it should work in ways where you can easily say, \"Run this for 10 hours,\" and then similarly, \"Checkpoint every 1 hour,\" and \"Show me a graph,\" or \"Eval everything against the previous 2 hours.\""
One clock, recorded by Etude on every row and checkpoint with no author code, usable everywhere a clock name is: (1) a training job's `until` ("run this for 10 hours"); (2) the training code asking whether a checkpoint is due every 1 hour on it (one small method on the tracked run, beside saving); (3) a report axis; (4) seats, e.g. `Earlier(clock=..., by=2)` with at-or-before ("against the previous 2 hours"). Values in hours. Today `WALL_CLOCK = "wall_seconds"` (etude.run.records) is a report axis only: "wall time since the run first started", not on checkpoints; replace it rather than add a second wall clock (one word per concept), and give it a plain name such as `hours`.
Meaning, recommended and open for the demo: the learner line's running time, summed over its attempts and continuations, excluding gaps between attempts and the parent's time before the continued checkpoint is counted once (absolute across continuation, like `updates`). So "10 hours" survives preemption and a resumed run continues the count. Old checkpoints without it: derive from `wall_ms` where possible, else it is absent for them.
